source.title: Rethinking Generalization in American Sign Language Prediction for Edge Devices with Extremely Low Memory Footprint
source.authors: A. Paul; P. Mohan; Stuti Sehgal

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Tests ASL classifiers with different augmentation methods and reports held-out and separate noisy-background dataset accuracy, extending generalization evaluation to a tiny edge-device setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports accuracy for its trained models and interpolation augmentation. It does not test arbitrary-label fitting or the claim versions’ mapped conditions; its separate generalization dataset is out-of-distribution, which the claim excludes.
record.test_reason: The study compares augmentation methods and post-training quantization in an ASL CNN. Its accuracy results do not test any of V1–V8. Citing Zhang et al. and discussing generalization do not establish a test of memorization capacity or the other specified claims.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusions about interpolation augmentation reducing quantization loss and improving generalization, including Model 2's 98.84% test accuracy and 74.58% separate-dataset accuracy. The authors additionally conclude that float32 inputs and outputs give the best results, without providing numerical comparisons for that conclusion.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a small ASL image classifier, Adam, and a comparison of image augmentation methods and post-training quantization; it does not test the claim’s arbitrary-label or mapped conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Augmentation method and model precision (float32 versus int8).

fits_no_version.finding: Interpolation-augmented Model 2 achieved 74.58% accuracy on the separate noisy-background dataset, versus 70.97% for Model 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation augmentation can improve accuracy on a separate noisy-background ASL dataset in this classifier.

fits_no_version.finding: Test accuracy fell from 98.53% to 95.28% after quantization for Model 1, versus 99.02% to 98.84% for Model 2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interpolation augmentation can reduce accuracy loss from post-training integer quantization in this ASL classifier.

record.peer_reviewed: IEEE Recent Advances in Intelligent Computational Systems; post-print of an IEEE RAICS 2020 paper
record.problems: The authors caution that 25 sample images provide little insight. The generalization dataset is separate and from a different distribution; the paper does not test arbitrary-label capacity. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep or test-error comparison beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or local-connectivity intervention.
Adam is used without an optimizer comparison.
No dropout comparison, including removal with weight decay under augmentation.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurements or comparison with generalization gaps.
No memorization estimates or retraining after removing memorized versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reason for excluding these results is the absence of the comparisons specified by V1–V8, not a blanket exclusion of distribution-shift evaluations. The 25-image caution concerns illustrative predictions, not the full test or generalization evaluations. No uncertainty estimates are reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not train on random labels or test the same recipes’ natural-label and random-label held-out performance.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No comparison with fully connected networks or analysis of local connectivity.
Uses Adam but does not compare optimizers.
No sharpness, perturbation tolerance, or generalization-measure comparison.
